# Two Subglacial Lakes in the Canadian Arctic

## Introduction

This dataset contains the locations of the two subglacial lakes in the Canadian Arctic, as well as the evidence of lake existence based on ice elevation analysis.

## Content

- `subglacial_lake_locations.gpkg`: GeoPackage file in the NSIDC Sea Ice Polar Stereographic North projection (EPSG:3413) showing the locations of two lakes.
- `analysis*.ipynb`: Analysis for each lake. These Jupyter notebooks start by downloading ArcticDEM and ICESat-2 data and end with the visualization of the lake elevation change.
- Other files: auxiliary data needed to execute `analysis*.ipynb`, such as glacier outlines[1].

## Additional notes

To run the notebooks correctly, put all auxiliary data in the same folder where `analysis*.ipynb` are stored.

The details of the elevation change mode can be found in the associated publication[2], which can be accessed at https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-20-1699-2026.

## References

[1] RGI 7.0 Consortium. (2023). Randolph Glacier Inventory - A Dataset of Global Glacier Outlines, Version 7.0. NSIDC: National Snow and Ice Data Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/f6jmovy5navz
[2] Zheng, W., van Wychen, W., Li, T., & Yamanokuchi, T. (2026). Active subglacial lakes in the Canadian Arctic identified by multi-annual ice elevation changes. The Cryosphere, 20(3), 1699–1714. https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-20-1699-2026
